posts.name: Amnachaidh
posts.cooked:
From the Sentinels Tactics thread (not a cut, just stealing the disussion topic idea) -- who was the first hero you played in SotM, and what impression did it give you?

My first game was - rather unwisely - as Absolute Zero. I saw how things could come together at a very low level, and we won on the strength of the other players. It was first edition, so there was no "H" mechanic, so my dead weight didn't gravely cost the team. I didn't get the full awesome of AZ, but I also saw that Wraith, Haka, Ra and Legacy were able to stomp the Baron into the ground.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
My first was a two player game with two heroes (like many people, I missed the section of the rules that says this isn't a good idea). I played Tempest because he looked cool, and I think my boyfriend played Ra. 

We saved Insula Primalis from the ravages of Baron Blade. Yay!

Now I've told this story multiple times now but I was really expecting not to like it at all, being a person who doesn't like comic books or superheroes and predominantly plays Eurogames. A couple of turns in and I was completely hooked - there are enough decisions and the idea of working out the effects of my different options and assessing which is the best for this particular situation was very appealing to my Eurogamer side, and getting to smash someone's face in mercilessly appeals to pretty much everyone, right?

It just goes to show that sometimes my first impressions are utterly, completely wrong.

posts.name: Ironic
posts.cooked:
I played Bunker alongside Ra, Legacy, Tempest, and (most importantly to this story) Tachyon in an epic battle to keep Voss from invading Megalopolis.  During that game, Tachyon (played by my sister) and I developed a great running gag of her saying something interested or curious about some of Voss' mad science, and me yelling at her ("Oooh, I see, the clamps along the back of the skull must allow for remote control - but wouldn't that arrangement result in limited range?" "I'm just glad the range is still long enough he can't hear you telling him how to improve his minions!").  It was a great first game, with a couple of tense turns where it looked like we might get overwhelmed, then a quick board clearing, an Egyptian god blowing up a space ship, and Tempest frying his nemesis.

It was about two games later that I realized Bunker is effectively unplayable, beginning my longstanding love-hate relationship with that deck, and my interest in proxies and variants for it.

I didn't under Legacy's deck very well at first, and couldn't realize why I would play cards like Heroic Intercept or Lead from the Front. I remeber that my friend with was playing the Wraith got out a Utility Belt early on and thought the character was just awesome, since she could use Throwing Knives and Stealth every turn.

posts.name: Chaosmancer
posts.cooked:
My first hero was Mr. Fixer, and I loved it. The game was Fixer, Ra, Tempest vs Plague Rat... I think in Rook City. Some friends of mine had just gotten Rook City and introduced me to the game. I got dual crowbars, some style (I think grease monkey), and harmony and just laid a beatdown on the rat for most of the game (I think we were misreading crowbars and allowing me to hit the same target twice). I felt awesome, even if I wasn't able to change things up much, but building a 1 point hit into a 8 pt hit every turn was so much fun.

 

This game was also were I first saw Ra burn himself to a crisp with Flame Shield, and I went down not long after, leaving Tempest with the Cleansing Downpour barely hangning on long enough to pull a lightning slash and a victory.

 

Loved the game enough that I eventually scoured the webs and my bank to buy "all the things" and now play solo (stupid work schedule)

posts.name: Under3
posts.cooked:
As I have mentioned my first hero was Absolute Zero, as soon as I opened the box and had a quick look at the decks he was the one who instantly leapt out at me as the one I really wanted to try first; everything about him just seemed more interesting at first glance than the others both visually/thematically and in gameplay with the clear damage redirection and strange base power.
The game was with one other friend, and I can't remember who else was played, against Baron Blade in Megalopolis (even though thematically Omnitron was my favourite villain from the base game but the high hit points and potential to hang around made me wary to try for the first game). I didn't find him too tricky, I was perhaps lucky to get through some decent card draws, and setting off his damage rebounding combos was great fun, he is still easily my favourite to play when he goes well.

After that I tried playing as him against Omnitron on Wagner Mars Base and realised the utter pain of how badly his deck can be shut down with what felt like constant red dust and technological singularities.
But I still love the guy.

posts.name: Julia
posts.cooked:
Pwatson1974 ran the first Sentinels game I ever played in, and forever shall I remain grateful for it. This was back in the 1st Edition days, about a month before Rook City came out. The game was Citizen Dawn in Atlantis. I believe we had Tempest, Visionary and Ra already at the table, and I chose Fanatic, because she looked so very badass with her wings armour and sword and all that.

I had the obligatory 'Why am I hitting myself?' moment, but then I understood that, while Fanatic may go down (in flames!), she will make damn sure that the villains go down with her! From that point onwards I had so much fun that she became my go-to character for a while.

As for my first game, I believe we all got our butts kicked by the Kraken in the end, but I didn't mind at all. I spent the next two weeks tracking down my own copy of the game, and the rest is history (and I can't believe that it has only been two years!).

posts.name: defeateddust
posts.cooked: My first game was with EvanDan55 and it was just before rook city came out. I used Legacy because he was the guy in front so why not go with what i though was the main character. I imediatly fell in love with the game though i couldnt afford my own copy till much later. Now I have my own copy of the game a large group of friends who love to play it, and legacy is still my favorite.

posts.name: grysqrl
posts.cooked:
I played Wraith along with one other person who didn't know how to play, taught by a third person who appeared very knowledgeable but, it later turned out, had never played before. We stomped on Omnitron in Silver Gulch, only to figure out later that Omnitron probably should have flipped over at some point (i.e. every round). We followed it up with two two-player games against Apostate with heroes who had little chance at getting through the DR once his relics were set up (I don't remember them all, but Scholar and Expat were in the mix).

Then I immediately grabbed up everything I could and actually learned how to play.

posts.name: Donner
posts.cooked: My first character was Tachyon.  We had Ra, Absolute Zero, Legacy, and Visionary.  I thought Tachyon was awesome, moving so fast.  And when I later switched to Haka, I felt so slow....  That game was pretty epic.  Baron Blade at Megalopolis.  Visionary was getting beat down (was at 16 health) and Baron Blade had 16 cards in his discard on his Impulsion side.  Then Visionary sacrificed herself to save the world (Brain Burn!).  We then beat the Baron handily before he could recoup.  We still talk about that save by Visionary.

posts.name: Mezike
posts.cooked:
The first hero I was given to play was The Wraith v Blade, followed by Fanatic v Voss in the second game. To be honest I really struggled to see the point of it all in those first two games. With The Wraith I had a ton of cards in hand and everything seemed a bit too easy, then with Fanatic not much happened and it didn't feel like I was being effective (particularly since one of my friends was having a whale of a time with Ra!) But I could see potential, particularly with how the game owner was wielding Tachyon. That, and a strong recommendation from someone whose opinion I really trust, was enough to encourage me to get the base game, and since the first two expansions were going cheap at the same seller I plumped for those as well. It's odd that Sentinels is one of my most favourite games ever when I didn't really enjoy those first games very much, but I am so glad that I trusted my instincts!

When teaching the game myself I usually give newbies an overview of what it's like to play some of the decks and then encourage them to go with whatever hero they like the idea of the most. There are a couple of Maths teachers in our game group and one of them took to Absolute Zero straight off the bat so you never can tell what the 'right fit' hero is for a first time player!

posts.name: charlotteML
posts.cooked:
When I first played the guy who owned the game (everything including promos up to Vengance at that point) had laid out all the heroes, villains and environments to let us have a look and I instantly noticed Unity, mostly due to her being a brunette with what I thought would be some type of engineering/technical skills. We ended up playing a five player game against Dawn (Owner as Ra, me as Unity, other completely new player as eternal Haka, someone else I can't remember what they played and then Ab Zero)

 

I enjoyed Unity throughout the game (I think her art and flavour text is what made me fall in love with the game) and we did end up winning although I think our team work left a little to be desired (me playing mr chomps the round before Haka did a rampage, a player who killed off one of the citizens when we were trying to get Dawn to flip back. Also a first round quote from the owner of the game: "Wait, you three ALL picked the version of your heroes who can't deal damage?! Hmmm, ok...") I didn't quite get a chance to set up a huge amount of damage but did contribute consistently throughout the game.

posts.cooked: Unity is my weakness character, right now. I would play her way out of proportion. The quotes + the huge damage you can do if you have your army of bots together + Mr. Chomps just works for me.

posts.name: Nielzabub
posts.cooked: My first game was a teamup with Reckless where I was Bunks, and we were fighitng the Baron in Megalopolis. I’ve loved Bunks ever since. He can be a tank or a damage dealer. I loved his versatility when I first played him.

posts.name: TeslaRoyale
posts.cooked: My first game was with Reckless, Nielzabub, and Rapscalion back in original edition. They had played a couple games already so I asked what hero they didn't like because I was used to playing games with people who alway played the same characters or same group position.  I figured that way I wouldn't have to compete with people for heroes in future games.  They told me Visionary wasn't very good.  I took her, and shuffled her deck, as we prepared to square off with Omnitron.  I quickly came to like her deck control and then an "Electro Pulse Explosive" happened.  Everyone dropped what they had planned for their turns and started discussing what they could do to get DR or damage it.  I just looked down at my hand and see this card called "Wrest the Mind" that I had been reading for half the game trying to figure out what a target was and why I would ever want to take that much damage of my own for anything.  (When we first started we were really conservative with hit points and almost revered DR as the holy grail of effects.)  I just said, "Guys, I got this."  I throw it on the "Electro Pulse."  Reckless pulls out his Kindle and jumps on the forums to check that it was a legal move.  Then we go through the round and when the villian turn comes up he asks, "Alright so you want to redirect it the explosive and blow it up."  To which I respond with, "No, I want to hit Omnitron."  I hit Omnitron. Then he explains to me how the damage on "Wrest the Mind" works like an interupt and asks me if I want to redirect the next hit to the "Expolsive" and he tells me I will take some total amount of damage that I can't actually remember off the top of my head (I can't remember how many heroes we were using.)  I respond with, "It's a three to one damage exchange rate!  I will gladly take that."  And from then on she has always been one of or depending on the day my favorite character.
